title: Sky Core can place a Prime Agent into conservatorship to make losses whole
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.4 grants the Prime Team discretion over how to rectify an RRC incident, then bounds it: "this discretion is exercised subject to the authority of Sky Core to impose penalties and take corrective measures, up to and including the conservatorship of a Prime Agent, to protect the ecosystem and make any losses whole."

Conservatorship is the escalation that makes the rest of the risk-capital regime credible. Penalties price a shortfall, but a Prime facing losses larger than its equity has no incentive left to respond to pricing — at that point only removal of control protects the ecosystem. Naming the power in advance also means using it is an Atlas-sanctioned procedure rather than an improvised emergency, which matters for a framework that treats ad-hoc deviation as misalignment.

The stated purpose is doubled: "protect the ecosystem" (forward-looking containment) and "make any losses whole" (backward-looking recovery). The second implies conservatorship reaches the Prime's capital, not merely its operations — consistent with risk capital existing to absorb losses rather than to signal seriousness.

The structural reading is a graduated ladder over the same incident: automatic per-second accrual, then verified reconciliation and finalised penalties, then corrective measures, then conservatorship. Prime autonomy is real at the low rungs and disappears at the top, and the Atlas is explicit that it is one continuum rather than separate regimes.
description: The ultimate corrective measure sits above Prime discretion over risk-capital incidents, so autonomy over rectification strategy never extends to unilaterally deciding the ecosystem absorbs the loss.
